transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m barely sleeping in any way that feels useful anymore. I’ll lie there awake replaying client models in my head, and then I’m up again at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach tight. By the time I go to work, it feels like I never actually rested.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things?
I’m not sure I’d say it’s about many different things. It’s more like my mind gets stuck on whatever is in front of me, and I have trouble turning it off.
Did these sleep problems start after a specific stressful event?
Yes. It started after the merger at work, when they reorganized our Caribbean-market division. That was about three years ago, and the sleep problems have been going on since then.
Do these sleep problems happen mainly when you’re thinking about the changes at work?

Mostly, yes. It’s when I’m thinking about the work changes and the client models—my mind just keeps going. I’ll lie there replaying things, and even if I fall asleep, I’m up at 3 or 4 with my stomach tight. Then I go into work feeling like I didn’t really rest at all.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yes. Most days I feel pretty down. I can be at work or just at home in my apartment, and there’s this heavy, gray feeling. I’m doing what I’m supposed to do, but it feels like I’m just going through the motions… and sometimes if someone asks me a normal question, I have to try not to cry.
Have you been feeling down nearly every day?

Yes… nearly every day. It’s just this heavy, gray feeling most days, whether I’m at the office or home. I get through what I have to do, but it feels like I’m just going through the motions, and sometimes even a normal question can make me feel like I might cry.
When you feel down, is it mostly tied to thoughts about the work changes, or does it also come over you when work isn’t on your mind?

It’s not only when I’m thinking about work. Work can set it off, but the heaviness is there most days anyway. I can be in the office or just sitting at home in my apartment, and I still feel gray and like I’m just moving through things. Sometimes even a normal question from someone makes me feel like I might cry.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to that, I guess. I know I feel down a lot, but I can’t clearly say whether I’ve stopped enjoying things.
Have you been getting less pleasure from things you usually enjoy?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t been paying close attention to pleasure, exactly. I know I feel down a lot, but I can’t say clearly whether things feel less enjoyable or if I’m just… not noticing much either way.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low in energy?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really been tracking my energy that way. I know I feel weighed down a lot, but I can’t tell if that’s the same as being unusually tired.
Lately, have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

I’m still not sure how to answer that. I haven’t really noticed it clearly one way or the other. I know I don’t feel great most of the time, but whether I’m enjoying things less specifically… I can’t really say.
Have you been feeling hopeless?

Yes… I think so. Most days I just move through work and then my apartment with this heavy, gray feeling. It feels like I’m going through the motions, and sometimes I’m just trying not to cry if someone asks me something normal.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I can say clearly. I feel really low a lot, but whether it’s that life isn’t worth living or harming myself… I haven’t really sorted that out.
Have you had thoughts about being better off dead?
I’m not sure. I don’t have a clear answer to that. I feel really worn down and low, but I don’t know if I’d put it as thinking I’d be better off dead.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes. It’s been pretty bad. Spreadsheets that used to be automatic for me now take hours. I lose track of what I’m doing, reread the same assumptions over and over, and even then I’m worried I missed something obvious before a presentation.
Have you been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself moving or talking slower than usual. No one’s mentioned it to me, either.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear change. My appetite seems about the same, as far as I can tell.
Have you been feeling worthless?
Yes. I do feel that way a lot. Like if my manager questions one of my projections, I immediately take it as proof that I’m not as sharp as I used to be, and that everyone can tell I’m failing.
Have you been feeling slowed down in your body or thoughts, like it takes more effort to move or think than usual?

Yes, more in my thoughts than my body. At work, spreadsheets that used to be automatic now take me hours. I lose track of what I was doing, reread the same assumptions over and over, and still feel like I’ve missed something obvious before a presentation.
Have you ever gone for several days needing much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t remember a stretch where I needed much less sleep and still felt energized.

Although symptoms began after a work-related stressor and insomnia is prominent, the low mood is not limited to thinking about the stressor and appears pervasive across settings, supporting a depressive episode over adjustment disorder or primary insomnia. Generalized anxiety is less supported because worry is not described as excessive across multiple domains.
